title: Why Cut Apples Turn Brown in 5 Minutes 🍎
description:
Why do cut apples turn brown? Slicing an apple bursts its cells, so the enzyme polyphenol oxidase meets the apple's polyphenols and oxygen, turning them into brown pigment, and lemon juice slows it down.

topic: Why do cut apples turn brown?
script:
Why does your apple grow a brown scab in 5 minutes?
Inside every apple cell,
two things are locked in separate rooms.
One holds an enzyme, polyphenol oxidase.
The other holds natural chemicals called polyphenols.
When you bite or slice the apple,
you burst thousands of cells.
The two finally meet,
and oxygen from the air rushes in.
The enzyme uses that oxygen
to turn the polyphenols into brown pigment,
like the melanin in your skin.
Scientists think it's a defence,
a brown shield against germs and bugs,
just like a scab on your knee.
Want to stop it?
Squeeze on some lemon juice.
Its acid slows the enzyme down,
and its vitamin C grabs the oxygen first.
So when your apple turns brown,
is it rotting, or healing?
Tell me in the comments.
key_facts: Cutting or biting bursts apple cells, letting the enzyme polyphenol oxidase (PPO) meet the apple's polyphenols, which are stored in a separate compartment
With oxygen from the air, PPO turns polyphenols into quinones that link into brown melanin-like pigments
Browning starts within minutes of cutting
Scientists think the browning helps protect the fruit against microbes and insects
Lemon juice slows browning: its acid slows the enzyme and its vitamin C (ascorbic acid) acts as an antioxidant
